research_question: In adults with severe mental illness (bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or other psychotic disorders) treated in community or outpatient settings, does collaborative care improve mental-health-domain health-related quality of life (SF-12/SF-36 Mental Component Summary or WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain) compared with usual care at the follow-up closest to and no later than 6 months?
outcome_description: Mental-health domain health-related quality of life at the follow-up closest to 6 months and no later than 6 months, taken as an endpoint (post-intervention) mean and SD per group rather than change from baseline. One score per trial: SF-12 or SF-36 Mental Component Summary (MCS), or the WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain. Physical component/domain scores, overall or total quality-of-life scores, symptom scales, functioning scales and satisfaction scales are not eligible. Randomised group sizes are used when analysed Ns are not reported; SEs or 95% CIs are converted to SDs using the group n. Follow-ups at 12 months or longer are not used.
positive_direction: A positive Hedges' g means collaborative care produced better mental-health-related quality of life (higher MCS or WHOQOL-BREF psychological domain score) than usual care.
search_queries: collaborative care severe mental illness randomised controlled trial quality of life
collaborative care bipolar disorder schizophrenia outpatient trial outcomes
care management intervention psychotic disorder usual care comparison SF-36 mental component
inclusion_criteria: Adults with severe mental illness (bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder or other psychotic disorders) treated in community or outpatient settings
Randomised or controlled comparison of a collaborative care / collaborative care-like multicomponent care model against usual care
Reports some quantitative health-related quality-of-life outcome (any instrument, any country, any diagnosis mix) from which an effect size can be derived
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, editorial, opinion piece, theoretical paper, study protocol)
No comparison between a collaborative care condition and a usual-care control condition
No quantitative outcome data usable for an effect size (no means+SDs, SEs/CIs convertible to SDs, t/F values, proportions or odds ratios)
Completely unrelated to collaborative care for severe mental illness
moderators_to_extract: Quality-of-life instrument (SF-12 MCS, SF-36 MCS, WHOQOL-BREF psychological)
Primary diagnosis group (bipolar vs schizophrenia/psychotic vs mixed)
effect_size_note: Pool as Hedges' g (SMD), collaborative care minus usual care, computed from endpoint means and SDs per group. Convert reported SEs or 95% CIs to SDs using the group n; use randomised group sizes when analysed Ns are unavailable. One effect size per trial, from the follow-up at or nearest below 6 months.
